reader.requirement: The two code characters stand before every report record of the report, outside the line description (COLUMN 1 is the first position after them) but inside the logical record size, so a RECORD clause's size is the code plus the line, in every RECORD form (fixed, range, VARYING), for every report sharing the file.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 refuses the identifier-1 operand (COBOL2713); 2002+ accepts it
below 2002 literal-1 must be exactly two characters (1985 SR1); 2002+ any length
ConstructRegistry report-code-is-2002: the word IS after CODE refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)
CODE reserved at all four editions

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the GR2 arithmetic (LineWidth = record size - code length; image = code + line) is edition-neutral; only the operand forms differ (85: a two-character literal only)

reader.notes: ResolveReports sets LineWidth = RecordClause.Upper - Code.Length (with no RECORD clause, the widest line), and PresentLine writes _code + Compose(). The COBOL2713 text for the identifier refusal says 'CODE IS literal-1' although 1985 prints no IS: a wording slip in a diagnostic, not a conformance defect.

refuter.evidence: Degenerate record sizes the reader did not try. r7r3-001: FD RECORD CONTAINS 3 CHARACTERS, RD CODE "AB", DE COLUMN 1 PIC XXXX VALUE "WXYZ" -> record 'ABW' (3 = code + 1 line column; correct). r7r2-001: RECORD CONTAINS 2 CHARACTERS -> record 'ABW' (od -c: A B W \r \n), 3 characters in a file whose every record has 2 positions. r7r1-001: RECORD CONTAINS 1 CHARACTERS (the code cannot fit at all) -> accepted with no diagnostic and writes 'ABW'. Same at --std 2023 (r7r1-002, r7r2-002: 'ABW'). Cause in code: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/ReportSectionBinder.cs#ResolveReports line 3812-3813 `model.LineWidth = ... ? Math.Max(1, record - (model.Code?.Length ?? 0)) : widest;` -- the clamp to 1 adds a print-line column the logical record does not have whenever record size <= 2. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR2 ("are included in the logical record size"); OK §1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR1; OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR3 ("Integer-1 specifies the number of character positions contained in each record in the file"). kb/Work: PB2519 and PB1934 (landed) name the same line but for the RECORD format arms, not the clamp; no note found for the clamp. SIBLING (another rule, 1985-FMT-XIII.3.2.2): the 1985 report FD format (rendered PDF page 589, folio XIII-7) admits only RECORD CONTAINS integer-3 and integer-4 TO integer-5; §1985:XIII.3.2.4 GR3 limits the clauses to those 'shown on page XIII-7'. r7var-001 RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 3 TO 6 on a report FD compiles and runs at --std 85 (under-rejects); the reader's p12var relied on it and its requirement wrongly ranged over a VARYING form 1985 does not admit for a report file.

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer, minor, degenerate sizes): with CODE and a RECORD clause whose size is 2 the record must be the code alone (2 positions: code included in the logical record size, line width 0), and a size of 1 cannot hold the code at all (refuse, or at least never write past the record); the compiler writes a 3-character record in both. Cause (b): the same at --std 2023. Repro: FD RPT RECORD CONTAINS 2 CHARACTERS REPORT IS R-A. RD R-A CODE "AB". 01 DE-A TYPE DE LINE PLUS 1. 02 COLUMN 1 PIC XXXX VALUE "WXYZ". -> expected record 'AB', observed 'ABW'.
